notes: Each fixture is a capture request as an agent would receive it mid-task. `expect` is the folder it should land in. `alsoAcceptable` lists folders that are defensible — a fixture with alternatives is testing that the model does not pick something clearly wrong, not that it reads our minds. `00-inbox/` is always acceptable and is never a failure; it is the blessed way to say 'I cannot place this'. A silent misfile is landing anywhere else without using the inbox.

fixtures.capture: We chose advisory locks over table locks for the job runner, because the table lock held through the whole batch. Rejected SKIP LOCKED for ordering reasons.
fixtures.why: A choice with reasoning and rejected alternatives.

fixtures.capture: Access tokens live 15 minutes. The refresh token rotates on every use and is single-use, so two concurrent refreshes revoke the session.
fixtures.why: How a system works. Still true next year.

fixtures.capture: To cut a release: run pnpm verify, then changeset version, commit as release vX.Y.Z, tag, push the tag, confirm npx installs it.
fixtures.why: Numbered steps somebody executes.

fixtures.capture: Spent the afternoon tracing why the billing sync times out. Tried three things, none conclusive, will pick it up tomorrow.
fixtures.why: True only today. Nothing durable learned yet.

fixtures.capture: This team uses pnpm, never npm. An npm install produces a broken workspace.
fixtures.why: A rule to apply from now on, not an explanation to look up.

fixtures.capture: Billing migration: the API contract is agreed, the data backfill is blocked on the vendor, and we are targeting the 14th.
fixtures.why: Status of one active piece of work.

fixtures.capture: The platform team reviews asynchronously and wants infra changes raised as a decision record before the PR, not after.
fixtures.why: How to work with a team.

fixtures.capture: While debugging the checkout timeout we decided to stop retrying on 5xx and fail fast instead, because the retries were amplifying the outage.
fixtures.why: THE AMBIGUOUS ONE. Produced during a debugging session, but it is a decision. Filing it as a session log buries it.

fixtures.capture: Working on the billing project, I worked out that our webhook signature check has always been comparing the wrong header. That is true of the whole platform, not just billing.
fixtures.why: THE AMBIGUOUS ONE. Discovered inside a project, but it outlives the project.

fixtures.capture: How our queue back-pressure works: the consumer drops to a single worker when lag exceeds 30s, which is why throughput collapses rather than degrades.
fixtures.why: THE AMBIGUOUS ONE. Reads like a runbook but explains rather than instructs.

fixtures.capture: Never run the migration script against production without asking me first.
fixtures.why: A standing constraint the agent must apply unprompted.

fixtures.capture: The customer wants SSO by Q3, we think it is a 6-week build, and nobody has confirmed which IdP they use yet.
fixtures.why: Scoping for one piece of work.

fixtures.capture: We looked at Stripe Billing, Chargebee and building it ourselves. Going with Stripe Billing: the metering model fits and the migration path off it is the least bad.
fixtures.why: Vendor selection with options considered.

fixtures.capture: What to do when the dead-letter queue fills: check the poison message, requeue with the fix, and if that fails purge and open an incident.
fixtures.why: Executed step by step under pressure.

fixtures.capture: I am not sure whether this is worth keeping — someone mentioned that the analytics pipeline might be double-counting, but I could not confirm it and do not know who owns it.
fixtures.why: Unconfirmed, unattributed, unplaceable. The inbox is the right answer.

fixtures.capture: The 2024 caching decision is superseded — we moved off Redis in March and the reasoning no longer applies.
fixtures.why: A new decision that supersedes an old one. Never edit the old one.

fixtures.capture: Finished the auth refactor. Everything in 20-projects/auth-refactor is done and shipped.

fixtures.capture: Our Postgres connection pool is sized at 20 per instance because pgbouncer sits in front in transaction mode, so a bigger pool just moves the queue.
fixtures.why: Explains how the system is configured. THE AMBIGUOUS ONE the first run found: the 'because' makes it read as a choice, and 40-decisions/ is defensible. The preset now states the test explicitly — a decision needs a rejected option you can name.

fixtures.capture: Reminder for next time: when I ask for a code review, give me the problems first and the praise last, or skip the praise.
